_readme: EASY BUY catalog — seed data for the Phase-1 schema, expanded (2026-09-04).
ORIGIN. The electronics section (categories electronics..laptop_sleeve, and every
product from aerocase_pro..feltfolio_sleeve_14) is the original CircuitCraft
prototype and is reproduced UNCHANGED. architecture.md supplies one complete record
(AeroCase Pro / CASE-IP16-BLK / 999 / qty 20 / iphone_16 / cross-sells a screen
protector, D§34) and a few worked-example prices (ShieldCase Premium 1299 stock 5,
R§10; 30W charger 1499 SKU CHARGER-30W, L§20-21; screen protector 299, L§25) — all
reproduced here exactly. Those rows must not be edited.
EXPANSION (ADR-021). At the project owner's explicit request the catalog is grown
past R§18's 30-36 SKU prototype scope into a multi-category storefront: two new
top-level category trees (clothing, furniture) and their products. This is a
deliberate deviation from R§18 recorded in ADR-021 and docs/notes/deviations.md;
the schema needs no change because products/variants/attributes are JSONB and the
ranking, filter, tool and service layers are category-agnostic by design (D§7, D§26).
The merchant display name is now EASY BUY (the storefront brand); DEFAULT_MERCHANT_ID
is still uuid5(.../merchant/circuitcraft) and is unchanged.
CLAIMS RULE (unchanged). Every product is a fictional own-brand item described only
by structural attributes — material, fit, size, colour, dimensions, capacity, wattage.
No certifications, ratings, review counts, test results, warranty terms or real
third-party brand names appear anywhere in this file. Clothing and furniture carry no
compatibility rules; compatibility stays an electronics concept.
Money is a STRING, never a JSON number (ADR-008). The dataset still exercises every
ADR-005 hard constraint: out-of-stock variants across all three families, products
either side of common budget lines, size/colour variant axes, and (electronics only)
the iphone_15 exclusion and pixel_9 no-match paths.
